top_story.headline: A negative $83,210.54 receipt from UBS Financial Services appears on Darrell Issa for Congress's books
top_story.dek: The FEC record carries no description for the reversal, and the filing itself doesn't say why it was made.
paragraphs: An itemized receipts entry (Schedule A) for Darrell Issa for Congress shows -$83,210.54 with counterparty UBS Financial Services Inc, dated March 31, 2026. FEC's convention is that a large negative amount marks a voided, reversed or refunded transaction. The description field on the record is blank, so the filing doesn't say what was reversed or why.
That is all the record shows. Whether the entry reflects a returned contribution, a corrected earlier entry or a movement of committee funds can't be determined from it. Transaction record.

Separately, today's batch includes a Form 99 that tripped the 'fraud' keyword scan. On a full read it is a rambling statement from Jason Changkyu Kim about his own election-fraud claims, not a compliance disclosure (see Form 99 Correspondence).

sections.headline: Eight Form 99s: mostly 'below the $5,000 threshold' notices ahead of the October Quarterly, plus one rambling political statement
paragraphs: No new RFAI letters surfaced in this edition's window, and no filings carry a sitting-lawmaker tag. Most of the eight Form 99s are small campaigns telling the FEC they haven't reached the $5,000 raising/spending threshold that triggers regular reporting, ahead of the October 15 quarterly deadline. One is a free-form political statement that hit the 'fraud' keyword scan, and one has no text at all.

items: For the Reform of the Great American Continent. Coalition for Electoral Reform: Jason Changkyu Kim (Toms River, N.J.), received 10/10. Keyword hit: 'fraud'. The one-page text is not a campaign-finance disclosure. It is a rambling statement listing Kim's claims and grievances: an 'Election Fraud' dispute with Donald Trump, references to the Republican National Committee, a suit against the State of New Jersey, and proposals on university meal plans and school lunch programs, including a figure of $6,408 to feed one student for four years. It contains no finance figures, and the 'fraud' hit comes from Kim's own election-fraud allegations. Filing.
Arthur Kennedy Alk (Democratic presidential candidate, Ozark, Ala.), received 10/11. Says he has not received over $5,000 in fundraising or spending. Filing.
Ayden Scott for Congress (Ayden Tate Scott, unaffiliated House challenger, Utah, Syracuse address), received 10/11. States the campaign has not met the $5,000 threshold. Filing.

Catalano for America 2028 (Joseph Samuel Catalano III, independent presidential candidate, Tampa, Fla.), received 10/11. States that as of September 30, 2026 the committee has not raised or spent more than $5,000 and has not met the reporting threshold for the October Quarterly Report. Filing.
Craig H Johnson II (Senate candidate, Grand Rapids, Mich.), received 10/11. Says he has not reached the $5,000 threshold and notes a $2,000 self-donation in the October quarterly period. Filing.

Donegan for Congress (Ann Marie Donegan, Democratic House challenger, Ohio, Olmsted Falls address), received 10/11. States the committee has not raised or spent more than $5,000 in the third quarter of 2026. Filing.

Jason Fistick for OH 03 (Jason Fistick, independent House candidate, Columbus, Ohio), received 10/10. The one-page Form 99 contains only the committee header and address; there is no message text. Filing.

Lam4Aloha - Adriel for Congress (Adriel C. Lam, Republican House challenger, Hawaii, Kaneohe address), received 10/10. States the committee has not met the $5,000 reporting threshold for the 2026 October Quarterly Report. Filing.
